items.title: World Bank Explores USDC Payments With Circle and Citi
points: World Bank is working with Circle (a stablecoin issuer) and Citibank to explore USDC (a cryptocurrency pegged 1:1 to the US dollar) payment capabilities for cross-border settlement
Testing likely focuses on improving cross-border transaction speed and reducing settlement costs
Represents institutional validation of stablecoins as viable infrastructure, potentially encouraging other development banks and governments to follow suit
Partnership model combining a multilateral development bank, fintech platform, and traditional bank may become a template for future institutional crypto integrations

items.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography for Ethereum Wallets
points: Researchers propose combining EIP-8141 (programmable account validation, letting each wallet pick its own signing method) with EIP-8288 (recursive STARK aggregation, a proof technique compressing multiple signatures) so the network verifies one proof instead of each signature separately

Efficiency varies widely across five post-quantum candidates on Apple M4 Pro hardware: FORS fits 100 signatures into 298 KiB, Falcon-512 fits 32, ML-DSA-44 fits 6, and standard Raccoon-128 fits only 1 signature per proof

Raccoon-G exceeds the 268M-word witness cap (memory footprint allowed per signature proof), requiring Merkle-tree-style recursive aggregation across five sub-proofs per signature, producing a 333 KiB root proof plus 2.84 KiB auxiliary data for 100 signatures

items.title: Multidimensional Fee Markets vs. Single-Resource Metering on Ethereum
points: EIP-7999 delivers 4%-34% more execution gas per block than the best one-dimensional fee alternatives while holding state growth (total size of blockchain state data) to 120 GiB/year, versus 56.7-96.0 GiB/year for single-resource approaches

Against an EIP-4844-style one-dimensional fee market based on blob transactions at a 4/5 target-to-limit ratio, EIP-7999's max-throughput setup adds 19.5M-56.2M gas per block while keeping near-limit block rates below the 38.8%-40.8% produced by that approach
Supports Ethereum's shift from separate metering (tracking resources individually) to separate pricing (charging differently per resource) to enable higher throughput as the network scales

items.title: Crypto Venture Capital's Structural Challenges
points: A $15 billion LP (limited partner, institutions funding venture funds) dinner highlighted that a $2 billion crypto-only fund targeting 3x returns needs $6 billion in gains, a bar once clearable via Layer 1 blockchain and infrastructure bets but now harder as value shifts to app-layer projects with existing user bases

Venture consensus expects crypto-only funds to have one or two more investment cycles before merging into broader frontier tech, with large VCs expanding into robotics, physical AI, and compute infrastructure

Near-term opportunities cited: AI-native companies adopting on-chain infrastructure for agentic payments and trading, DeFi platforms not yet at millions of users, and tokenized equities (blockchain-native stock ownership) in emerging markets lacking traditional brokerage access

items.title: Wells Fargo Doubles Bitcoin ETF Holdings
points: Wells Fargo's reported BlackRock Bitcoin ETF (IBIT) holdings doubled to 49.58 million shares worth $2.35 billion as of September 30
This makes Wells Fargo the largest reported holder among investment managers tracked
Reflects Bitcoin's 42% price gain between June and September

No wallet backups or security credentials were compromised in the breach
